name: A stuck machine says so
summary: The designer ruled that a machine which cannot carry out its order stops where it stands, shows a visible distress state, and resumes when the way clears — never improvising, never failing silently (S-10, from Q-85). The robots shipped before that state existed, so a mark-1 blocked on a rock currently looks identical to one that has finished its list and to one that is broken. This adds the missing piece: a reportable reason on the actor, a status frame on the machine sheets, and the same sound-and-glance treatment the player's own blocked tap gets.
requirements: A blocked actor carries a reportable refusal reason, produced by the same sim path that already answers the player's blocked taps
A status frame on the machine sheets — the bot sheet needs a cell it does not have today
The distress state is visible at a glance on a tablet without reading, per the wordless rule
A sound and visual cue of the same weight the player's own blocked action gets (the standing any-actor-gets-the-player's-treatment rule)
The machine resumes on its own when the obstruction clears — no player intervention needed to un-stick it
Sim-level test: a bot ordered onto an unreachable tile enters distress deterministically and leaves it when the path opens; the replay reproduces both transitions
current_status: Filed 2026-09-03 on integrating the Q-85 ruling. Nothing built yet. The reason plumbing largely exists — the sim already produces refusal reasons for the player's own blocked taps — so the real cost is the sheet cell and the presentation pass. Blocked on nothing: it is buildable today.

plan.step: Record the ruling as a settled decision (S-10) and annotate the queue entry
Surface a refusal reason on the actor when its order cannot be executed
Generate the status frame for the machine sheets through the art pipeline
Wire the presentation: sprite state, cue sound, and the resume transition
Sim test for the distress enter/leave transitions, verified through a replay
